claims.text: The base alloy is equiatomic Nb-Zr-Ti-Hf-Mo, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
The base Nb-Zr-Ti-Hf-Mo alloy is a disordered BCC solid solution.
The base alloy has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
The base alloy has limited room-temperature compressive plasticity.
The proposed intervention replaces 20% of the original Mo content with Ta, producing approximately Nb20Zr20Ti20Hf20Mo16Ta4 in atomic percent.
Partial replacement of Mo by Ta will reduce the alloy's overall electronegativity difference.
Mo introduces strong directional bonding in this alloy.
The Mo-induced directional bonds impede dislocation motion and reduce plasticity.
Replacing part of the Mo with Ta will weaken the directional bonding and facilitate dislocation slip.
The modified alloy will remain a chemically homogeneous, disordered BCC solid solution.
Refractory solute atoms can contribute strength through solid-solution strengthening.
The Ta-modified alloy will maintain a room-temperature compressive yield strength near 1700 MPa.
The Ta-modified alloy will show a 20-30% increase in room-temperature compressive plastic strain relative to the base alloy.
Arc melting followed by homogenization at approximately 1200 °C for 1-2 hours will ensure complete mixing and chemical uniformity.
The beneficial strength-plasticity effect is limited to Ta substitutions around 20% of the original Mo content.
Substitution levels outside the proposed range may cause phase instability, secondary-phase formation, or unwanted strength loss.

contradictions.description: The alloy is described as maintaining an overall equiatomic composition or equiatomic balance, but replacing 20% of the 20 at.% Mo fraction with Ta gives Nb20Zr20Ti20Hf20Mo16Ta4, which is not elementally equiatomic.
